title: Anthropic Stands Alone as Rest of US IPO Market Slows to a Crawl
source_used: Bloomberg (text read via Yahoo Finance UK, which carries the Bloomberg report)
key_facts: A mix of risks threatens to stall the US IPO pipeline, leaving Anthropic's potential debut as one of the few offerings investors can count on.
Oura and Bamboo Insurance Services postponed plans as interest rates climbed and the Iran war dragged on; SB Energy and Nscale filed publicly but have not begun formal marketing.
Anthropic is seeking to match or exceed SpaceX's record debut as soon as next month, in a listing that would dwarf the other potential deals combined.
Citigroup's Aloke Gupte said it is the first pause this year; JPMorgan's David Bauer pointed to rising uncertainty before the 3 Nov midterm elections.
In September only five sizable companies went public, raising $1.9 billion, the slowest month since March, as 10-year yields jumped more than 50 basis points.
US IPOs have raised $163 billion this year, more than three times last year; 7 of the year's 10 largest deals trade below their IPO prices.
